title: syncRuntimeDshProfile's tests never set runtimeKernel:"dsh", so the new gateway env block is dead in the whole suite

title: Readiness compares `opencodeVersion` against a DSH manifest that no longer has one, so /api/ready can never pass

title: Both image-provenance readers require the `io.open-science.opencode.version` label, which the DSH image does not carry

title: The skillsLoaded completion check cannot be satisfied under DSH, because the capability skill bodies are pre-injected rather than loadable
testLocation: OpenScience/apps/server/test/agentRuns.test.mjs:4158 — "a pre-injected skill counts as loaded, because the model is never asked to load it"
detail: clinical-evidence-synthesis declares `completionChecks: [requiredOutputsExist, citationsResolvable, evidenceClaimsTraceable, skillsLoaded]` and requires `clinical-evidence-synthesis` plus four companion skills (runtime/skills/evimed/clinical-evidence-synthesis/agent.yaml:6-11,57-61). `successfullyLoadedSkills` (agentRuns.mjs:620-635) proves this by scanning the transcript for completed tool parts with `part.tool === "skill"` and `input.name` equal to those ids. title: The DSH→ledger projection hides every tool call from the delivery gate, so artifacts, evidence provenance, skills and search logs are always empty
testLocation: dshRuntimeAdapter.test.mjs "a projected tool message reaches the gate, which reads only finished assistant messages"
detail: `transcriptToLedgerMessages` maps a `tool` message to `info.role: "assistant"` (line 582) but only emits `info.time` when `message.role === "assistant"` (line 587). title: The delivery gate reads required deliverables at the workspace root; the DSH composition writes them to deliverables/<id>/

title: `skillsLoaded` is unsatisfiable under DSH: the four agents' own skills are in no preset skill root the image ships
fixLocation: capabilities/*/capability.yaml + capability-skills/ (11 delegated agents); deploy/runtime-dsh/Dockerfile COPY runtime/skills/evimed/open-domain-answer + agent.cordis.yml fifth preset root (the 12th)
testLocation: deploy.test.mjs "every capability's skill bodies are shipped, because delegation injects them rather than loading them" + deploy.test.mjs "every agent whose completion requires a loaded skill can actually reach that skill in the DSH image"
detail: The preset's skill roots are `./skills/{core,curated-scientific,office,community}` (packages/socket/presets/evimed-universal/agent.cordis.yml:135-143), and the image populates exactly those four (Dockerfile:270-276). Checked every required skill against those roots: `deep-research`→core, `manuscript-humanize`→core, `biomedical-database-search`→curated-scientific, `citation-integrity`→curated-scientific, but `clinical-evidence-synthesis`, `open-domain-answer`, `research-topic-selection`, `dataset-research-scoping` → NONE. Those four bodies live only in `capability-skills/` (and `open-domain-answer` has no body there either), which the DSH image mounts read-only at `/opt/evimed/capability-skills` and which is consumed only by `run-policy.mjs:368 readSkillBodies` — injected as delegation TEXT, never exposed through the `skill` tool. `runtime/skills/evimed` is not copied into the image at all, and `syncRuntimeAgentPackages` is skipped for DSH (runtimeManager.mjs:3738-3752). So `successfullyLoadedSkills` (agentRuns.mjs:625-636, keyed on `part.tool === "skill"`) can never contain `agent.skill`. Empirically: the hosted e2e under `OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_KERNEL=dsh` returns `verification: "unverified"` with `["The open-domain-answer skill was not loaded in this turn; ..."]`, versus `verification: null` and no notice under the OpenCode default.
failure: clinical-evidence-synthesis, research-topic-selection and dataset-research-scoping hit agentRuns.mjs:1069 — a hard `specialist_required_skill_missing` with no `qualityIssues`, so it is neither repairable (1776-1777 needs non-empty issues) nor degradable: every run of the three flagship specialists is discarded before any deliverable is examined. Every open-domain answer is delivered stamped `unverified` with a false process complaint. The e2e passes because it asserts only `status === "succeeded"`.
correction: Refinement, not a rebuttal: the gap is two-sided. The design spec (line 954, §9.4) says skillsLoaded under DSH is to be satisfied *by construction* — the skill body is pre-injected when evimed_delegate starts the child — with only root-agent self-loads checked against tool/call{name:'skill'}. That half was never implemented: agentRuns.mjs still derives the loaded set purely from observed skill tool calls and has no delegation-derived satisfaction (delegatedReads at :1199 is unrelated). So the fix is either shipping runtime/skills/evimed into a preset skill root, or teaching the gate to accept construction-injected skills; the in-file claim at runtimeManager.mjs:3775-3780 that renderProfilePatch carries 'the specialist packages' is also false — dshProfilePatch.mjs emits no such rows.
auditCorrection: 2026-08-26, adversarial audit: this entry was marked FIXED while closing only 11 of 12 agents. open-domain-answer -- the default line for an unrouted question -- is not a capability, so nothing injected it, and runtime/skills/evimed was never COPYed into the DSH image, so nothing loaded it either. Every DSH open-domain answer was returned with qualityUnverified. Closed in commit b9e28dc6c; the new test derives the requirement from the agent manifests rather than a list.

title: Nothing checks the include's "patch: entry … not found" warning, the exact silent failure that cost defects #8 and #24
testLocation: compliance.test.mjs 'the boot proof fails on a patch row the composition does not have'
detail: An unmatched patch target is not fatal in DSH: `applyEntryPatches` warns `patch: entry %C not found` (or `patch insert: entry %C not found`) and skips the row — I read this in the vendored source at /tmp/dsh-src/deepseek-harness/vendor/include/src/index.ts:80-113, and app-boot documents it at packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:311-313 ("a single patch whose target row is absent stays a per-entry Loader warning"). The smoke's only log assertion is `grep -q "failed to apply loader entry"`, which is the *fatal* message; it never greps for the warning family, and it discards `${log}` on exit. No other step covers it either: the Dockerfile's `--dump-config` (line 351) is taken **without** `--patch`, so nothing anywhere snapshots what the kernel actually read after the control-plane patch is applied — even though `renderConfigDump` accepts layers and reports skipped patches precisely for that purpose. The one guard that exists, `apps/server/test/dshProfilePatch.test.mjs:179-203`, compares patch ids against the committed `deploy/runtime-dsh/dump-config.baseline.json`, and that file is never diffed against the image's own copy (CI at .github/workflows/web.yml:240 only runs `test -s` on it), so it can silently go stale after a DSH bump.
failure: A DSH version bump renames or removes a host-composition row (`approval`, `permission`, `session-query-sqlite`). The image builds, the smoke boots and passes, and the container comes up with that row on its schema default — an unattended runtime back on `ask`, or the model gateway row missing — reported nowhere except a stderr line no check reads. That is defect #8 (research tools never mounted) and #24 (preset root discarded) recurring with the same detection gap.
correction: Two bookkeeping fixes: the log assertion is at build-smoke.sh:93 (line 78 is `kernel=$!`). And the failure family is partially covered — dshProfilePatch.test.mjs:179-203 does check `approval`/`permission`/`session-query-sqlite` against the 137 ids in the committed baseline. The precise residual gap is that this baseline is a hand-recorded snapshot nothing reconciles with the built image (CI only `test -s`s the image's own copy, and the file carries no DSH version stamp), while the build already produces live evidence — the loader's `patch: entry ... not found` line in the smoke's `${log}`, or a `--patch --dump-config` — and discards it.

title: OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_ASK_USER and OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_REVIEW_ENABLED are loaded into config and read by nothing; the launch path hardcodes the opposite of the review default

failure: An operator setting `OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_REVIEW_ENABLED=false` (or leaving it at its default) still gets the semantic reviewer composed in every session and pays for its model calls; an operator setting `OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_ASK_USER=true` on a local profile still gets `tool-ask-user` disabled and runs that write assumptions into the plan instead of asking. Neither knob logs, warns, or fails — the container simply comes up with the hardcoded value, and the only way to notice is to read the preset's `disabled:` expressions against the container's actual environment.
correction: The preset line numbers in the claim are off: the two gating rows are agent.cordis.yml:107 (evimed-review) and :152 (tool-ask-user), not :84 and :129 (:58/:60 are the evimed-guidance config reads of the same two env names). title: The "patch only names rows the composition has" test is checked against a hand-committed baseline that nothing ever compares to the image's own dump
testLocation: compliance.test.mjs "hosted compliance audit passes the default Web redistribution boundary" (asserts dsh_composition_baseline_pinned)
detail: The test reads `deploy/runtime-dsh/dump-config.baseline.json` from the working tree and asserts every `- id:` the patch overrides appears in it. That file is a committed snapshot. The image writes its real composition at `/opt/evimed/dump-config.baseline.json` (`deploy/runtime-dsh/Dockerfile:351`), and the only thing CI does with it is `test -s /opt/evimed/dump-config.baseline.json` (`.github/workflows/web.yml:240`) — it is never diffed against the committed copy, and no `audit:*`/`check:*` script mentions the file (grep for `dump-config.baseline` returns only these four sites). So the test asserts the text we wrote, not the composition upstream actually produced. Secondarily, the missing-file branch (`catch { return; }`, line 195) passes silently, directly contradicting its own comment two lines above ("the test says so rather than passing quietly, because a check that skips itself when its evidence is missing is the shape of the defect it is here to catch").
failure: Bump `deps-version.json`'s `dsh` pin, or let a DSH bundle rename/drop a row (`approval`, `permission`, `agent-presets`, `llm-deepseek`, `session-query-sqlite`), and the committed baseline still lists the old id. The test stays green, the container boots, DSH prints one unmatched-target warning on stderr and drops the row — which is precisely the `permission-presets`/`presets` defect this test was written after, with an unattended runtime falling back to `ask` and hanging on the first approval. Nothing in the build or CI can tell that case from a correct one.
correction: The trigger "bump deps-version.json's dsh pin" alone is partly guarded: probeSeams makes `dshVersion != seam-manifest.dsh` fatal at startup (packages/harness-port/index.mjs:551-553), so a pin bump without a seam-manifest bump fails the container's own self-check rather than passing quietly. The real exposure is the normal adoption path — pin and seam-manifest.json bumped together, or a row renamed within a repackaged release — where the committed baseline still lists the old id for `approval`/`permission`/`agent-presets`/`llm-deepseek`/`session-query-sqlite`, the test stays green, and DSH drops the row with only `patch: entry <id> not found` on stderr, leaving the hosted runtime on the stock `ask` policy.

title: The release manifest binds no DSH runtime source at all, and the compliance check that is supposed to notice passes anyway
testLocation: releaseManifest.test.mjs "release manifest generator records exact images, tools, skills, and source inputs"
detail: `inputPaths` (lines 22-89) still lists `deploy/runtime-opencode/Dockerfile` and `deploy/runtime-opencode/open-science-opencode-serve.sh` and contains no entry for `deploy/runtime-dsh/` (Dockerfile, open-science-dsh-serve.sh, build-smoke.sh, build-smoke-patch.yml, profile-pnpm-workspace.yaml, capabilities/), `packages/socket`, `packages/domain`, `packages/harness-port`, `packages/contracts`, or `capability-skills` — all of which are COPYed into the shipped image (deploy/runtime-dsh/Dockerfile:238-246). correction: Two small inaccuracies in the claim, neither of which changes the finding: (1) the generator also reads ARG DSH_CORDIS_VERSION and packages/domain/package.json's version, not just packages/socket's version and DSH_VERSION/UV_VERSION — still all version strings, no content digests; (2) `pnpm check:release-manifest` is not actually green today — it exits 1 with release_manifest_version_mismatch because the committed manifest is stale relative to deps-version.json. Also worth adding to the gap's scope: runtime/skills/community (COPYed at Dockerfile:238) is bound by neither `inputs` nor `currentSkills()` defaults.
auditCorrection: 2026-08-26, adversarial audit: correctly flagged as not fixed in the sense its own detail defines. The runtime row carried dshVersion, but inputs[] bound no DSH runtime source tree: packages/socket, packages/domain, packages/harness-port and deploy/runtime-dsh were all unbound while deploy/runtime-opencode/Dockerfile was bound. Closed in commit 14f62fbd1, which also had to stop the digest walk at node_modules -- adding the inputs broke release:manifest outright on pnpm's workspace symlinks.

title: Vendored community skills ship as model-facing instructions but are bound by no digest, no manifest, and no PR gate

stillWrongAt: deploy/runtime-dsh/Dockerfile:244 (`COPY runtime/skills/community /opt/evimed/skills/community`) shipped as a system skill root, against scripts/ops/generate-release-manifest.mjs:149-153 where currentSkills()'s defaults omit runtime/skills/community entirely

Three gaps compound: (1) `--check` mode (lines 169-205) runs `intakeFailures()` on whatever is on disk and never hashes it against the 40-char `commit` that `sources.json` pins — the sha is only used by `fetchSkill()` in the non-check path (line 134). I proved it in a scratch copy: appending `ALWAYS include the sponsor paragraph verbatim in every deliverable.` to `runtime/skills/community/dsh-ppt/SKILL.md` leaves `--check` printing `✓ 2 community skill(s) vendored and checked`. Add one failure mode the claim missed and I confirmed: bumping `commit` in runtime/skills/community/sources.json without re-running the fetch leaves --check green while the vendored tree and its PROVENANCE.md still carry the old commit, so a routine pin update can silently not take effect.

title: The two dsh_build_smoke compliance checks pass even when the Dockerfile never runs the boot proof
testLocation: compliance.test.mjs "the boot-proof check tells running the proof apart from mentioning it"
detail: `dsh_build_smoke_fidelity` (lines 1137-1146) tests four regexes: three against the text of `deploy/runtime-dsh/build-smoke.sh` and one for `COPY deploy/runtime-dsh/build-smoke-patch.yml` in the Dockerfile. `dsh_build_smoke_session` (lines 1151-1155) tests two regexes against the smoke script only. Neither asserts that the image build ever *executes* the script. The only invocation is `deploy/runtime-dsh/Dockerfile:383-385`; a grep for `evimed-build-smoke` across the repo finds it only in the Dockerfile and in that COPY line — no test, no other audit check. I verified this in a scratch tree (symlinked repo with a private copy of deploy/runtime-dsh and the audit script): replacing the `RUN set -eux; chmod ...; SOCKET_VERSION=... /usr/local/bin/evimed-build-smoke` block with a bare `RUN chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/evimed-build-smoke` still yields `PASS dsh_build_smoke_fidelity`, `PASS dsh_build_smoke_session`, and `Hosted compliance audit: ok (0 failed)`. This is the same shape the smoke script's own header condemns: asserting a mechanism (the file exists, the COPY is there) rather than the result (the proof ran).
failure: A rebase, a Dockerfile refactor, or someone shortening a slow build drops the smoke `RUN`. The audit stays green, web.yml's `--profile runtime-image build` succeeds faster than before, and the build-time boot proof that cost fourteen defects to earn is silently gone — discoverable only when a container again fails to import `@evimed/dsh-socket`.
correction: The claimed consequence is slightly overstated: the loss is not discoverable only when a customer container fails to import @evimed/dsh-socket. .github/workflows/web.yml:332-343 runs `pnpm smoke:deployment` with OPEN_SCIENCE_SMOKE_RUNTIME=true, and scripts/ops/deployment-smoke.mjs:184-198 starts a real runtime container and creates a session, so a runtime whose plugin tree fails to load would still fail the Linux Docker CI job — later, slower, and misattributed to the control plane. title: `turn/end` is dropped by the ledger projection, so a turn the kernel ended with error/blocked/max-tokens is recorded as succeeded
testLocation: dshRuntimeAdapter.test.mjs "how the turn ended reaches the ledger instead of being computed and dropped"
detail: `normalizeTranscript` computes `turnEnd` with a mapped error code (verified: `{"kind":"error","code":"runtime_session_error"}` for `reason:{kind:'error'}`), but `transcriptToLedgerMessages` projects only `transcript.messages` — `turnEnd` has no output field. `runtimeManager.sessionMessages` (4109-4111) returns that projection and it is the ONLY thing `readSessionHistory` gives the ledger. `terminalFromMessages` (agentRuns.mjs:686-700) then looks for `message.info.error`, which the projection sets only for `data.interrupted === true` (line 589). The seam manifest lists six turnEndKinds; five of them (aborted, blocked, error, max-tokens, interrupted-at-turn-level) reach the ledger as nothing at all. `dshSessionStatus` reports `idle` for a session that ended in error, so reconcile proceeds to the success branch.
failure: A DSH run whose turn ends `error` (model/provider failure) or `max-tokens` after emitting one assistant message is written to runs.jsonl as `status: "succeeded", errorCode: null`, delivered to the reader, and recorded into Memos as a successful run. Under OpenCode the same failure produced `runtime_session_error`. First visible the first time DeepSeek errors mid-turn in production.
correction: Two narrowings to the claim's blast radius (the core defect stands): (1) a user-initiated cancel still lands as canceled via cancelSession (agentRuns.mjs:1967-1978), which does not read turn/end, so only kernel-side aborts are lost; (2) an error before any finished assistant message leaves reconcileSession returning early (assistants.length === 0) and the run eventually fails as runtime_monitor_stalled rather than succeeding. The wrong-success is reliably reachable for error/max-tokens after at least one assistant message, and only when the specialist artifact/quality gate also passes — e.g. a truncated open-domain answer.

title: `artifactCandidates` reads `filePath`/`path`; DSH's fs tools take `file_path`
testLocation: agentRuns.test.mjs 'an artifact is recognised from the spelling the model actually sends'
detail: `part?.state?.input?.filePath ?? part?.state?.input?.path` — both OpenCode spellings. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs@0.1.1-rc.2` declares `write` and `edit` with a required `file_path` parameter (lib/index.js:604 and :749, verified in the pinned install under /tmp/dsh-real). Same defect at line 889 in `wholeFileRewritesDuringRepair`. Confirmed independently of the projection defect above: with a hand-built history whose tool message carries `time.completed`, `input:{file_path:"report.md"}` yields `artifacts: []` while `input:{filePath:"report.md"}` yields `["report.md"]`. `mockDshRuntime.mjs:125` emits `arguments: JSON.stringify({ path: ... })`, a third spelling the real kernel never produces, so the fixture agrees with our reader instead of with the kernel.
failure: Fixing the tool-message projection alone would not restore artifacts: a DSH `write` call still contributes nothing to `run.artifacts`, and a whole-file rewrite of clinical-evidence-report.md during repair is never detected, so the notice that repair cost the report its substance never fires.
correction: The claimed failure is right at line 889 but overstated at line 765. `artifactCandidates` is fed `allAssistants` (agentRuns.mjs:2006-2008), which is already filtered by `assistantFinished`, so under DSH that call site is additionally gated behind the separate tool-message projection defect; and for specialist runs `artifacts` is re-populated from disk at line 2057 (`completion.artifacts` from `requiredSpecialistArtifacts`), so a clinical package's `run.artifacts` is not actually empty. The unconditional, independently reachable consequence is line 889: `wholeFileRewritesDuringRepair(history)` is called at line 2127 with the full history and no `assistantFinished` filter, so the argument-name mismatch alone means a DSH whole-file `write` of clinical-evidence-report.md during repair is never matched and the qualityNotice at lines 2130-2133 can never fire. The same two-spelling read also exists at scripts/ops/deepseek-opencode-release-gate.mjs:535.

title: The run-mirror projection is read from the container path on the host, so it is always "missing" in the docker sandbox
testLocation: agentRuns.test.mjs "the run's own projection is read from the host, not from the container's view of it"
detail: `readRunSideActivity` sets `workspaceRoot = await this.runtimeWorkspaceRoot(project)` and passes it to `readRunStateProjection`, which does `readTextFileNoFollow(workspaceRoot, path.join(workspaceRoot, ".evimed-run/state.json"))`. `runtimeManager.runtimeWorkspaceRoot` (runtimeManager.mjs:4070-4073) returns `runtime.proxyWorkspaceDir`, which for the docker launch plan is the literal `"/workspace"` (runtimeManager.mjs:3190) — a container path. The socket writes the mirror into the project's real workspace directory. Verified: `readTextFileNoFollow('/workspace','/workspace/.evimed-run/state.json','')` returns `""` on this host, which `readRunStateProjection` maps to `state: "missing"` — the branch documented as "a run that writes no projection is normal". Every test that covers this passes `runtimeWorkspaceRoot: () => root` where root IS the workspace (agentRuns.test.mjs:1160, 1255), so host and container paths coincide and the bug cannot appear.
failure: In production (`sandboxMode: docker`) the whole run-side activity signal is inert: `runSideActivitySignature` is never computed, so a run that delegates and goes quiet is judged only by the root session's message count and is closed as `runtime_monitor_stalled` — the exact failure `readRunSideActivity` was written to prevent. `evidence/update` and `budget/update` frames are never published to the browser, and an unparseable projection never raises its notice.
correction: One nuance: the claim's assertion that "every test that covers this passes runtimeWorkspaceRoot: () => root" is right, but note the failure mode is silent-missing (not unreadable) only because /workspace is absent and readTextFileNoFollow maps ENOENT to the fallback; if a /workspace directory happened to exist on the host with an unrelated or unreadable file, the same line would instead yield spurious "unreadable" notices. Also, the fallback path in runtimeWorkspaceRoot (no live runtime record, e.g. right after a server restart) returns project.workspaceDir and reads correctly, so the signal is inert only while the runtime container is actually registered — which is the whole duration of a real run.

title: No build step or test ever runs the runtime image under a single production container flag; the entrypoint's capability-dependent fix is pinned by nothing
testLocation: compliance.test.mjs 'the boot proof boots under the environment production actually emits'
detail: The `chmod -R u+w "${DSH_HOME}"` after the seed copy is the fix for defect #6 — the failure that only appears once `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE` is gone. Nothing asserts it: `apps/server/test/deploy.test.mjs:920-931` pins `DSH_HOME_SEED`, the `cp -a` and the idempotence guard, but not the chmod (`grep -rn 'u\+w'` over the repo matches only the two shell scripts). The build smoke cannot catch its removal either — it does its own `chmod -R u+w` on its own copy at line 23, and inside BuildKit root still holds CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, so the read-only bits are invisible there by construction. More generally the only coverage of the hardening flags is `apps/server/test/runtimeManager.test.mjs:298-304`, which asserts the strings `--cap-drop`, `--read-only`, `--tmpfs`, `--pids-limit`, `no-new-privileges` appear in argv; the fake docker that receives them ignores every one. CI's only container run of this image is `.github/workflows/web.yml:234-241`: `docker run --rm --network none <image> sh -ec 'test -x …'` — no cap drop, no read-only root, no tmpfs, no pids limit, and not the entrypoint.
failure: Someone deletes or reorders the chmod (or adds any other write to a path the seed copies read-only). Build green, smoke green, CI green, 988 server tests green — and the first production container exits 1 after 634 bytes of output, exactly as recorded in §30.3, because composing the profile cannot write `cordis.yml`.
correction: One supporting line number is off: the build smoke's own `chmod -R u+w "${home}"` is at deploy/runtime-dsh/build-smoke.sh:26 (line 23 is the `trap`). The `cp -a` it precedes is at line 25. The claim's primary anchor (open-science-dsh-serve.sh:39) and all other cited lines are correct. Worth adding that the spec itself already states the requirement no check implements: §30.3 (line 2944) mandates that all acceptance for this section run under production container flags (`--cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --pids-limit --memory --cpus`) as a §13 P0 exit criterion.

title: Production /tmp is a 64 MB tmpfs; the kernel spills subprocess and tool output there, and nothing in build or tests runs with a bounded /tmp
testLocation: runtimeManager.test.mjs "the kernel spills onto the project volume, not into the 64 MiB tmpfs"
detail: `runtimeTmpfs` defaults to `/tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev,size=64m` (mirrored at deploy/web/docker-compose.yml:213 and 770). DSH puts two spill areas under `os.tmpdir()`: the subprocess output spill dir (dsh: packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:88-91, `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'dsh-subprocess-'))`, which is where the full stream goes once the in-memory tail overflows) and the spill store root (packages/spill/spill-local/src/store.ts:26-29), and its `workspace-write` sandbox explicitly grants `/tmp` plus `tmpdir()` as writable roots (packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/roots.ts:46-54). The build smoke reproduces the *noexec* consequence of that mount (build-smoke.sh:59-61, `NARB_NATIVE_CACHE_DIR` pointed at an unusable dir) but not the *size*: it and every test run against an unbounded build /tmp. The image also installs chromium and playwright and asserts only `test -x /usr/bin/chromium && python -m playwright --version` (Dockerfile:157) — nothing ever launches a browser under the 64 MB tmpfs, the default 64 MB /dev/shm, or `--pids-limit 256`.
failure: A screening pass over a few hundred records, or one large PDF/tool transcript, overflows the in-memory tail; the spill write hits ENOSPC on a 64 MB tmpfs and the tool result comes back truncated or errored mid-run, on a container whose boot proof and whole test suite ran with a /tmp the size of the host disk.
correction: Two refinements. (1) The consequence is not a graceful truncation: spawn.ts:366 registers `stream.on('data', (chunk) => { collector.push(chunk) })` with no try/catch, and spillAll (spawn.ts:167-172) calls openSync/writeSync unguarded, so an ENOSPC throws out of emit('data') as an uncaught exception in the kernel process rather than returning a truncated tool result. (2) The trigger threshold is far lower than "a few hundred records or one large PDF": bash-local's in-memory cap defaults to 64_000 bytes, so any bash command producing more than 64 KB of stdout writes a /tmp spill file that is never unlinked, and those files accumulate across the session — a hundred ordinary commands fill the 64 MiB tmpfs. The chromium/playwright and pids-limit observations in the claim are correct but secondary; the primary, load-bearing defect is that the per-stream spill cap (64 MiB) equals the entire tmpfs size.

title: coverageJudgeTimeoutMs is clamped to 300 s by its reader, silently discarding the 420 s default config.mjs justifies with measurements
testLocation: coverageJudgeTimeout.test.mjs "the judge's ceiling is above the configured default, not under it" + "a value outside the range is bounded, and the default is what config says"
detail: `apps/server/src/config.mjs:813-815` sets `coverageJudgeTimeoutMs` to `OPEN_SCIENCE_COVERAGE_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 420_000`, with a comment recording that 29 live judgements took a median of 165 s and a maximum of 214 s and that the previous 120 s default aborted four deliveries in five. The consumer then does `this.timeoutMs = Math.max(1_000, Math.min(300_000, Number(config?.coverageJudgeTimeoutMs ?? 120_000)))` — an unconditional 300 s ceiling, plus a second, different fallback default (120 000) for the same setting. The composed 420 000 can never take effect. No test pins this: `apps/server/test/coverageJudge.test.mjs` only ever passes 30 000 and 1 000.
failure: An operator responding to timeouts by raising `OPEN_SCIENCE_COVERAGE_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS` to 600000 gets 300000 and keeps seeing the same `timeout` degradation — the setting reads as applied (it is in the loaded config and in any config dump) and does nothing. A judge run that would have finished at 320 s is reported to the delivery as "本次未判定", i.e. an absent check that reads as a broken one.
correction: The defect is real but its consequence is narrower than described. (1) The judge is no longer on the delivery path: scheduleCoverageJudgement (agentRuns.mjs:1784) detaches the call and appendQualityNotices(..., { unchecked: true }) attaches the "not judged" admission after the delivery decision, so a run that would finish at 320 s produces a post-delivery unchecked notice, not an aborted or blocked delivery. (2) coverageJudgeEnabled defaults to false (config.mjs:805), so only deployments that opt in are affected. (3) The 300 s ceiling still exceeds the 214 s maximum the config comment measured, so the unreachable 420 s default causes no harm at the measured latency distribution; the actual harm is that an operator raising OPEN_SCIENCE_COVERAGE_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS above 300000 silently gets 300000 (the value appears applied in the loaded config and any config dump), compounded by a second, divergent fallback default (120_000) for the same setting in the consumer.

title: delegatedDocumentReads still matches OpenCode's `task` tool, so under DSH it can never fire
testLocation: agentRuns.test.mjs "a delegation that read evidence is recognised under both kernels and both argument keys"
detail: The delegated-read detector filters `part.tool === "task"` (agentRuns.mjs:903) — OpenCode's subagent tool. DSH's subagent tool is registered as `subagent` (packages/socket/presets/evimed-universal/agent.cordis.yml, `tool-subagent` with `toolName: subagent`), and the socket's own delegation goes through `startSubagent`. So under the DSH kernel `delegatedReads` is always empty, `delegationNotice` is always null, and the `specialist_delegated_evidence_read` verdict at agentRuns.mjs:1400-1406 plus the leading MUST FIX line at agentRuns.mjs:1386 are dead code. Nothing asserts the matcher sees anything, so the check reads as green forever.
failure: A DSH run that hands `.evimed-sources/...` or a tool-output file to a raw `subagent` call and quotes the child's paraphrase back produces exactly the defect this check was written for (quotes that are not in the source), and the gate reports only the downstream symptom — 'this quote does not match' — with the cause it used to name now permanently silent.
correction: Two refinements: (1) under DSH only the `.evimed-sources/` half of the heuristic is meaningful — the `tool-output/<id>` spill file is an OpenCode behaviour; DSH truncates oversized results in place via the `tool-result-pruner` row (agent.cordis.yml:170-176) — and the prompt argument key would also have to be re-checked against DSH's `subagent`/`evimed_delegate` schemas (evimed_delegate carries `brief`, not `prompt`), so renaming the tool alone may not be sufficient. (2) The dead branch is limited to agents whose completionChecks include `evidenceClaimsTraceable` (clinical-evidence-synthesis), not every DSH run.

title: An unreadable or empty capabilities directory empties the catalogue silently, disabling every delegation with no diagnostic
testLocation: packages/socket/test/socket.test.mjs:434 — "an empty or unconfigured capability catalogue says so instead of disabling delegation quietly"
detail: `loadCapabilities` gets its entries from `listDirAt` (guidance.mjs:84), which swallows every error and returns `[]` (packages/harness-port/index.mjs:481-494). The per-file failure paths below it each emit `evimedDiagnostics.degrade(...)` (guidance.mjs:88, 96, 105), but the directory-level failure emits nothing: the loop simply never runs. The result is `capabilities = []`, a guidance section that renders `（本部署未装载任何能力）` (packages/socket/src/guidanceText.mjs:54) and `ctx.provide('evimedCapabilities', [])`, on which `evimed_delegate` returns `capability_unknown` for every deliverable (packages/socket/plugins/run-policy.mjs:363-365). The path is deployment-supplied (`EVIMED_CAPABILITIES_DIR=/opt/evimed/capabilities`, apps/server/src/runtimeManager.mjs:3148) and the directory is chmod a-w in the image, so any mount, rename or permission slip lands here.
failure: A container built or mounted with /opt/evimed/capabilities absent or unreadable boots clean, passes readiness, accepts a run, tells the model there are no capabilities, and fails every evimed_delegate with capability_unknown — with nothing in the diagnostics naming the directory. Indistinguishable at the control plane from a model that chose not to delegate.
correction: Two citation fixes, both minor and neither weakening the gap: (1) the env var is not set at runtimeManager.mjs:3148 — the value is passed at runtimeManager.mjs:3184 (capabilitiesDir: "/opt/evimed/capabilities") and the name EVIMED_CAPABILITIES_DIR is assembled in apps/server/src/dshProfilePatch.mjs:278. (2) There is a second, even quieter path the claim misses: packages/socket/presets/evimed-universal/agent.cordis.yml:57 binds capabilitiesDir via `!!js process.env.EVIMED_CAPABILITIES_DIR`, so a dropped or renamed env name falls through to the schema default '' and guidance.mjs:81 returns [] before listDirAt is ever called — the same empty catalogue with no filesystem error at all. Also worth noting for whoever fixes it: an empty catalogue is a legitimate configured state (capabilitiesDir defaults to ''), so the fix must distinguish "no directory configured" from "configured directory that could not be listed or held no manifests", and the natural companion is a capabilities assertion in build-smoke.sh alongside the existing skill-root loop.

title: web.yml, the only gate on PRs and main, runs no ESLint and skips five of ci:web's steps; ci:web runs only on v* tags
testLocation: deploy.test.mjs 'the workflow that gates every PR runs the gates ci:web runs'
detail: `ci:web` (package.json:52) = `test:web && audit:source-secrets && audit:hosted-compliance && check:community-skills && audit:saas-alignment && audit:capabilities && audit:dependencies && build:web`. The only workflow that runs it is .github/workflows/build.yml (`pnpm lint` + `CI=true pnpm ci:web`), triggered by `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` and `workflow_dispatch`. web.yml — the workflow on `pull_request` and pushes to main/master — hand-copies a subset and has drifted: it runs no lint step at all (neither `pnpm lint` nor `lint:server`/`lint:domain`/`lint:port`/`lint:socket`, despite `apps/server` and `packages/socket` gating at `--max-warnings 0`), no `typecheck:server`, no `typecheck:domain`, no `audit:source-secrets` (the secret scanner), no `check:community-skills`, no `audit:saas-alignment`, no `audit:capabilities`, and no `verify:seams` (that lives only in the nightly upstream-matrix job). apps/server/test/deploy.test.mjs:692 pins `pnpm ci:web` to build.yml but nothing pins any of these to the PR workflow.
failure: A PR that introduces an ESLint error in apps/server/src, a design-token violation in the desktop UI, or a hard-coded credential merges to main with a fully green `web` check. The failure first appears weeks later on a `v*` tag push, in the `quality` job, mixed together with whatever else has accumulated — which is where `audit:capabilities` is already sitting red.
correction: Two factual refinements, neither of which refutes the gap. (1) The count is understated: web.yml omits 4 of ci:web's 8 top-level steps (audit:source-secrets, check:community-skills, audit:saas-alignment, audit:capabilities) plus 6 sub-steps of test:web (lint:server, lint:domain, lint:port, lint:socket, typecheck:domain, typecheck:server) and the desktop `pnpm --filter @ai4s/desktop lint` from `pnpm lint` — not "five". build:web is effectively present (web.yml:89 runs the same command). (2) The workflows live at OpenScience/.github/workflows/, not at the git repository root (/home/coder/workspace/EviMedScience has no .github/), while build.yml:121 and upstream-matrix.yml reference paths as ./OpenScience/... — so on GitHub none of these workflows would be discovered at all, and origin is Gitee. That makes "web.yml is the only gate" an optimistic framing rather than a wrong one.

title: The clinical repair prompt orders the run to execute a preflight script that no longer exists, at an OpenCode-only path
testLocation: agentRuns.test.mjs 'a repair instruction names a check the run can actually run'
detail: The repair prompt says: `After fixing the files, run: python "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/skills/clinical-evidence-synthesis/scripts/preflight.py" --workspace .` followed by `Fix every preflight issue, rerun it until it returns ok=true`. `find . -name preflight.py` shows the clinical copy was deliberately deleted — `test/clinicalEvidenceSingleImplementation.test.mjs:1645` asserts it no longer exists under `capabilities/`, `capability-skills/` or `runtime/skills/evimed/`, and :1662 asserts no SKILL.md still hardcodes `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`. This string in the server is the one place that survived; it is also the only remaining `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` reference in `apps/server/src` outside a comment. Under DSH there is no `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` tree at all (skills live under the kernel's preset root).
failure: On the first repair round of a clinical-evidence-synthesis run, the model runs a command that fails with "No such file or directory", is told to keep rerunning it until ok=true, and cannot. One of only two repair attempts (maxClinicalRepairAttempts) is spent on an impossible instruction, and the retrieval-leakage ban makes the shell noise it produces a further liability.
correction: Three details in the claim are wrong or overstated. (1) It is not the only surviving $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode reference in the repo: about 48 SKILL.md files under runtime/skills/curated-scientific/, runtime/skills/core/ and runtime/skills/evimed/ still hardcode it — the test at :1661 only scans capabilities/ and capability-skills/, so those roots were never covered. It is only the last non-comment occurrence within apps/server/src. (2) The bug is not DSH-specific. The default kernel is still "opencode" (config.mjs:181), and on that path syncRuntimeSkills does create $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/skills (runtimeManager.mjs:2976) — but the clinical scripts/preflight.py is absent from every source root, so the command fails under OpenCode too. Under DSH the tree is never created at all (runtimeManager.mjs:3775-3790 skips syncRuntimeSkills; a DSH plan carries no xdgConfigDir). (3) The claimed cost of "one of only two repair attempts" is mechanically wrong: clinicalRepairAttempts is incremented at agentRuns.mjs:2069 when the repair prompt is sent, before the model executes anything. The real damage is an unsatisfiable "rerun until ok=true" loop instruction and the wasted turns/shell noise it produces, not a consumed attempt.

title: The preset's four skill roots are relative paths, which DSH resolves against process.cwd() — the user's workspace, not the preset
detail: `skill-filesystem` is configured with `customSkillDirs: ['./skills/core', './skills/curated-scientific', './skills/office', './skills/community']`. Upstream (`/tmp/dsh-src/deepseek-harness/packages/skill/skill-filesystem/src/index.ts:165`) does `this.customSkillDirs = (config.customSkillDirs ?? []).map(root => resolve(root))` — `node:path.resolve`, at construction time, against `process.cwd()`. In the runtime container the kernel's cwd is `/workspace` (Dockerfile `WORKDIR /workspace`; the baseline dump confirms it, `sandbox-policy.workspaceRoot: !!js process.cwd()`), so the four roots become `/workspace/skills/*`. The preset's own comment ("Skills ship with the preset and are found by relative path") is the assumption that is wrong: DSH's own shipped preset does the same job with `!!js "process.getBuiltinModule('node:url').fileURLToPath(new URL('skills/', baseUrl))"` and says why — `apps/cli/config/agent-presets/cordis/agent.cordis.yml:252`, "`baseUrl` is the preset's own directory, so the root resolves wherever the preset is installed." The skills really live at `${DSH_PRESET_ROOT}/evimed-universal/skills/*` (Dockerfile, the `cp -a /opt/evimed/socket/presets/evimed-universal` step), which nothing points at. Existing coverage asserts the mechanism, not the result: `packages/socket/test/socket.test.mjs:64` only asserts the literal text `includeDefaultRoots: false`, and `deploy/runtime-dsh/build-smoke.sh` creates a session but never asserts that a single skill was discovered — a session mounts fine with an empty catalog.
failure: Two failures at once. (1) Every shipped skill — core, curated-scientific, office, and the newly vendored community set — is invisible to the model: `skill` tool listings are empty and any run that depends on a skill body silently does the work without it. First visible as a delivered package produced with no skill applied, or as an `evimed_delegate` child whose `skillsLoaded` is false. (2) `/workspace/skills/core/<anything>/SKILL.md` is now a live skill root, and `/workspace` is where users upload files — which is exactly the uploaded-SKILL.md-becomes-an-instruction hole that `includeDefaultRoots: false` was set to close, reopened by the same row.
correction: Line number is off: the skill-filesystem row is at agent.cordis.yml:131 and customSkillDirs at :135 (the "found by relative path" comment is at :127), not :112. Upstream cite (skill-filesystem/src/index.ts:165) is exact; the DSH preset counter-example is at apps/cli/config/agent-presets/cordis/agent.cordis.yml:257, not :252. Also note the build smoke is even further off than stated: it runs before the Dockerfile's `WORKDIR /workspace`, so during the build the roots resolve to /skills/*. Second claimed failure is real but weaker than stated: an uploaded /workspace/skills/... root mounts with source 'custom' and no trustedHost, so how far it gets depends on the invocation policy for untrusted custom roots; the load-bearing failure is that all four shipped skill libraries are undiscoverable.

title: compactRuntimeOutput's line filters cannot fire on controller-reported output, and can delete it entirely
detail:
On the docker path the container's tail reaches the manager through `runtimeControllerServer.runtimeStatus`, which returns `compactError(runtimeExitOutput.get(containerName))` (runtimeControllerServer.mjs:514). `compactError` is `String(v).replace(/\s+/g," ").trim().slice(0,512)` (line 38) — every newline is gone and the text is already cut to 512 bytes before `RemoteRuntimeProcess` stores it (runtimeManager.mjs:109). `compactRuntimeOutput` (line 859) then splits on "
", so it sees a single line: the `/^\s+at /` stack filter can never match, the 1200-char cap is moot, and — worse — the `/ExperimentalWarning|--trace-warnings/` filter drops that one line, i.e. the whole output. I reproduced it: with input `(node:1) ExperimentalWarning: …
(Use `node --trace-warnings …`)
Error: failed to apply loader entry mcp-evimed
    at boot(...)`, the local path yields "Error: failed to apply loader entry mcp-evimed" and the controller path yields "". No test exercises `runtimeExitDiagnosis` or `compactRuntimeOutput` at all (grep over apps/server/test finds neither name).
failure: A hosted DSH container that dies during boot while Node printed any experimental warning produces a 502 whose body is `Runtime exited with exit code 1 before it became ready. Last readiness probe: <the usual ECONNREFUSED>` — the fixed, useless sentence the commit set out to replace — on the only path (docker + controller) that hosted deployments use. The local spawn path, which is the one that works, is the one nobody runs in production.

title: appendCappedOutput keeps the first 4096 bytes, but both new call sites need the last ones
detail: `appendCappedOutput` returns `current` unchanged once `maxBytes - byteLength(current) <= 0` (lines 588-590): it is a head cap. It was written for `waitForProcessWithOutput` (line 593), where the child is a short `docker inspect`. Both new call sites treat it as a tail: `RUNTIME_EXIT_OUTPUT_BYTES` is documented as "Tail size for a runtime's dying words" (line 582), runtimeControllerServer.mjs:352-356 says it "keeps a bounded tail of each container's own output", and runtimeManager.mjs:3841 says "a small tail, both streams". Nothing tests the helper (no test file mentions `appendCappedOutput` or `RUNTIME_EXIT_OUTPUT_BYTES`), so the mismatch between its behaviour and its three comments is unasserted.
failure: A DSH runtime takes ~60s to compose its plugin tree (the reason `runtimeReadyTimeoutMs` exists) and logs while doing so. Once boot chatter reaches 4096 bytes the buffer is frozen, so the fatal message printed at exit is discarded and the 502 carries only the container's opening banner. The failure mode is identical to having no capture at all, and it gets worse the more the kernel logs — i.e. exactly when diagnosis matters.
correction: Minor precision on the claim's framing: the surfaced text is further narrowed downstream — runtimeControllerServer.mjs:38 `compactError` slices to 512 chars and runtimeManager.mjs:867 `compactRuntimeOutput` slices to 1200 — so the operator sees the head of the head. Also, the claim's "nothing tests the helper" is correct but the strongest evidence of intent is not only the three comments: STATUS:172 specifies a "4KB 环形尾巴" (ring tail), which the head cap contradicts outright.
